text: 🇲🇽🌎 "Terrorism is something else. Calling them this way represents interference in our country." "That's why we made the amendment to Article 40 of the Constitution, because it cannot be a pretext for invasion, for interference by any country in our country." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 3, 2026 A reporter noted that Argentina had just declared several cartels, including Mexican ones, terrorist organizations, in line with US policy. Sheinbaum: "Here we call it organized crime, and we fight it, and we work every day for security and peace in our country."
banner: "IT CANNOT BE A PRETEXT FOR INVASION"

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "Now they are opinion-givers. But they no longer decide. Nor does the oligarchy decide Mexico anymore." "When Zedillo arrives, they abandon Salinas and go with Zedillo. When Fox arrives, they abandon Zedillo and go with Fox." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 3, 2026 The business council CCE called for an "independent" INE. Sheinbaum answered with the history of Mexico's electoral reforms, pushed by the democratic movement after the 1988 fraud against Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas. She said the real concentration of power in the INE came in 2014, under the Pacto por México, when the national councilors took over naming every state electoral councilor. The intellectuals who denounced the 1988 fraud were co-opted by Salinas, she said, and followed every president after him. "Democracy is the will of the people."

🔥🇲🇽 "In 2006, one of the biggest electoral frauds was carried out." "Why didn't they want to open them? Because that Electoral Tribunal and that Federal Electoral Institute knew that López Obrador had won." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 3, 2026 Reporteros MX played an interview in which Vicente Fox says of 2006: "Calderón won, or I can say it here, I made Calderón win, although it's not very democratic to say that." Fox added he would not have handed the presidential sash to López Obrador. Sheinbaum, who took part in reviewing the 2006 results, recounted the "vote by vote" mobilization, the 250,000-vote margin, a recount of only 8 to 9% of polling stations, and the burning of the ballots with PRI and PAN consent. "Today Fox comes to tell us that, in effect, he actively participated so that López Obrador would not win."

🇲🇽✊ "They are certainty for their families." — Zoé Robledo, IMSS Director General, Mañanera, Nov 3, 2026 One week into IMSS's 12 actions in 120 days: the 8% raise is paid to 565,000 active workers (Oct 27-28) and 370,000 retirees (Nov 1). In Campeche, 128 workers got permanent posts today, part of 10,939. Among them: a COVID-era doctor after six years of temporary contracts, and a cleaner who signed 15-day contracts for almost five years. The call for 2,500 specialists opened today, and 67 new mammography units are running. Weekend sessions did 561 surgeries in 20 hospitals. Night and weekend consultations start Nov 15 so December appointments aren't lost. "Today 113 days remain."

🇲🇽✊ "With this, we will have completed the rehabilitation and equipping of all of ISSSTE's operating rooms." — Martí Batres, ISSSTE Director General, Mañanera, Nov 3, 2026 ISSSTE presented its own 12 actions in 120 days. Already done in 2025-26: 710 new ambulances, 13 surgical robots (it had one), 4,078 new specialists, 7,605 workers given permanent posts and five new hospitals. By early March it will hire 1,710 specialists, 502 nurses and 250 general practitioners, and finish the last 55 operating rooms. It will buy 69 CT scanners, 53 mammography units, 7 MRI machines and a linear accelerator. It will remodel 64 emergency rooms, drop the paperwork check at ER entry, add 100 consulting rooms to the Universal Health Service and double telemedicine.
banner: ISSSTE: ALL OPERATING ROOMS IN 120 DAYS

text: 🇲🇽🔍 "It is a crime, what she committed. In her own personal accounts she received resources of illicit origin, and it is an investigation that we did not start." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 3, 2026 TV host Inés Gómez Mont was detained Oct 30 in Florida by US immigration authorities. The Attorney General's Office (FGR) says she has three Mexican federal arrest warrants: organized crime and money laundering, plus two for tax fraud. It says she received money diverted through shell companies from about 2.45 billion pesos in contracts with the federal prison agency, and omitted over 13 million pesos in taxes. Mexico requested her provisional arrest for extradition in September 2025. She is seeking asylum in the US, saying she is persecuted for conservative views.

🇲🇽🌎 "First, the government of Texas doesn't decide." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 3, 2026 Texas moved to claim nine islands and islets in the Río Bravo. Sheinbaum said islands form as the water moves, and the binational International Boundary and Water Commission measures which side they fall on: "If it's half and half, it's half and half. But that is decided in that commission." She added: "They are in elections and claim declaratively that these islands are already part of Texas, but no." Asked if it was electoral: "Yes, from my point of view."

🔥🇲🇽 "Mexico is a magnificent country, and what falls to us is to defend sovereignty in every sense. Sovereignty before external powers. And sovereignty, as Article 39 of the Constitution says, resides in the people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 3, 2026 "Fox today says two terrible things: that he took part in the 2006 election, and that governing Mexico is like governing a company, that it is a business. How is it a business? Yes, for them it was a business. For Marta Sahagún's sons, for all of them, it was a business." She recalled the 2024 vote: 36 million votes, two-thirds of both chambers of Congress and most state legislatures. "Because the popular will spoke. Many people don't like that."

🇲🇽💵 <u>Remittances: $47.2 Billion So Far in 2026, Despite Trump</u>

Mexico received $5.362 billion in remittances in September, according to Banxico data reported by El Financiero. That's the lowest in five months and 1.7% below August, but still up 1.6% from a year earlier. From January to September the total reached $47.164 billion, up 2.1% on 2025, despite deportations, ICE raids and Trump's remittance tax.
